inline_comments.comment: Typo: "marmaid.js" should be "mermaid.js". The same typo also appears in `.changeset/full-clubs-learn.md` and `.changeset/true-parrots-build.md` (line 5 in both).

The version bump type `major` is incorrect. In semver, `major` signals a breaking change. Adding a community integration documentation entry is not a breaking change. Per the contribution guidelines cited in this PR: "Changesets that add features should be `minor`". This should be `minor` (or `patch` since it is purely documentation). The same incorrect `major` bump also appears in `.changeset/true-parrots-build.md`.

This file is an exact duplicate of `.changeset/full-clubs-learn.md`. Having two identical changesets will produce two identical entries in the changelog. Only one changeset file per PR should exist. Please delete one of the two.

The `docs/` directory is auto-generated from `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` (the canonical source). The four extra sub-links added here — `Octave Repo Index`, `News`, `Function Reference`, and `Bug Tracker` — do not exist in the source file at `packages/mermaid/src/docs/ecosystem/integrations-community.md`. Editing the generated output directly means these entries will be silently overwritten the next time the docs are rebuilt. All desired sub-links should be added to the source file instead.

general_comments.comment: Three separate changeset files (`.changeset/7123.md`, `.changeset/full-clubs-learn.md`, `.changeset/true-parrots-build.md`) were created for a single change. This will produce three separate changelog entries and three version bump operations on release. A PR should have exactly one changeset. It looks like a manual file (`7123.md`) was created first, then `pnpm changeset` was run twice, producing two auto-generated files. The two auto-generated files and the manual file should be consolidated into a single changeset using the standard `adjective-noun-verb` naming convention. Also, the manually created file name `7123.md` (using the issue number) does not follow the project's naming convention for changesets.

The two documentation files are out of sync: `docs/ecosystem/integrations-community.md` has 5 sub-links under the GNU Octave entry while `packages/mermaid/src/docs/ecosystem/integrations-community.md` has only 1. Since `docs/` is generated from the source in `packages/mermaid/src/docs/`, the source file should be the single place where content is maintained. Decide on the desired set of sub-links and apply them only in the source file.
